title: Round 1 (patch 6): the combo ladder, x5 is a concert
why: Andre: combos need to feel like 'ooh yes I got a freaking 5x combo!'. In the baseline, x3, x5 and x9 looked about the same (a sky tint, some rings, a small side plaque). Direction: MORE; x1 keeps its flash, and every tier stacks a new kind of response on top.
changes: x3+: a centre-stage callout that slams in and grows each tier: SPARKLING, RADIANT, DAZZLING, BRILLIANT, PRISMATIC, LEGENDARY, TRANSCENDENT (rainbow).
x3+: a synthesized chord sting that climbs two semitones per tier; x4+ adds a sub boom.
x5+: nightclub lasers: 12 rainbow beams sweep up from the horizon behind the cabinet and hold while the chain lives.
x5+: tapered anime speed lines around the board, plus a hard 160 ms strobe in the tier colour (skipped with reduced motion).
checks: verify 22/22 (WebGPU)
WebGL2 fallback renders the lasers, 0 errors
nine-wave fixture reaches x9 with 0 errors on both builds

title: Round 2 (patch 7): Resonance music, a soundtrack that plays along
why: Andre: 'next up is ambient music'. The drop had no music unless you loaded your own file. Tetris Effect's trick is that the music layers in with your play.
beforeLabel: patch 6 (no music; the clip is silent)
afterLabel: patch 7 with the music the engine schedules for this exact run (turn the sound on)
changes: A generative, sample-free soundtrack on the music bus (the Music volume slider controls it), in your Gem tones key (natural minor), at 84 BPM.

Pad always on (chord every 2 bars: i VI III VII, then i iv VI VII). Bass joins as the board warms up, 16th arps through a tempo-synced echo as flow rises, then kick, hats and clap when the board is hot or a chain hits x4. A pentatonic lead plays while the x5 sky lasers are on.
Loading your own track silences it; removing the track brings it back. Mute works as before.
audio: 60 s journey render: calm, warming up, hot, a x5 chain with lasers (30 to 42 s), cooling down
images: Spectrogram of the journey: the pad from 0 s, the arp around 17 s, drums (vertical hat lines) from 23 s, the lead in the laser window, fading back after
checks: verify 22/22
offline render uses the real in-page scheduler (OfflineAudioContext): 558 notes in 60 s, 0 errors
live path: after one real click the realtime scheduler is producing notes (pad level 0.64 at 2.5 s)
not verified by ear: I cannot listen, so the musical taste is Tront's call

title: Round 3 (patch 8): the journey, zen/endless moves through stages
why: Andre: 'for zen/endless to also feel like progression you can switch up the stage/background/theme/music after each XX points', and 'animating the background so it feels like a journey'. Endless stays endless (Jennifer's favourite); the journey rides on top.
afterLabel: patch 8: the same move, now STAGE 2 TIDEPOOL
changes: Six stages, set by the shared score (so co-op partners always match): DAWN SHALLOWS, TIDEPOOL, EMBER REEF, AURORA DEEP, STARFALL, PRISM HEART, then ENCORE loops. Stage lines at 5K, 15K, 30K, 50K, 75K...; every stage is a little longer than the last.
Each stage grades the whole sky (a colour multiply plus a stage-coloured horizon glow) and crossfades over a few seconds.
Each stage changes the music: its own tempo (84 to 128 BPM) and chord progression family.
Crossing a stage line is a show: a stage card slides in under the board centre (so a milestone banner can share the moment), lasers, three world rings, eight fireworks and a frame light chase.
Under the score: STAGE n, its name and a progress bar to the next stage.
checks: verify 22/22
journey tour clip (tools/out/clips/r3-tour.mp4): all six stages plus ENCORE, each with a distinct sky, 0 errors
stage is a pure function of score, so both co-op screens show the same stage
videos: Journey tour: every stage line in turn (score jumped to each line every 2 s)

title: Round 4 (patch 9): gamepad support
why: Andre: 'add gamepad support'. Also part of the drag-fatigue fix: a pad (or the arrow keys) now plays the whole game without holding the mouse.
beforeLabel: before: no gamepad input at all (any clip; pads were ignored)
afterLabel: patch 9: a scripted standard pad walks the cursor, holds A + down to swap, then X hint and Y point
changes: Standard-mapping gamepads drive the board cursor: D-pad or left stick (with key repeat), tap A to select or swap with the selected neighbour, hold A + a direction to swap that way, B deselects or closes a panel, X hint, Y point ping for co-op partners, Start settings, Back/Select co-op room.
A bold pulsing gold cursor frame whenever the keyboard or a pad is driving; it turns aqua with swap arrows while A is held.
Rumble scales with the combo tier (x5+ and specials hit hardest), a short buzz on an illegal swap's bump, a long one on a stage change.
The first button press also wakes the audio, like a click.
checks: verify 22/22
scripted pad: cursor 27 -> 2 by D-pad taps, hold A + down swapped 2<->10 (1 move, +150), rumble fired, X showed a 2-cell hint, Y placed a point ping on the cursor cell, 0 errors
not tested with a physical controller here: needs a real pad on Tront's machine

title: Round 5 (patch 10): Flashes setting (comfort option, full juice stays the default)
why: aFoolsDuty: a sweet combo 'probably gave someone in the world an epileptic fit'. Tetris Effect has MIN, MID and MAX effect settings. Direction: comfort is an OPTION, the default never gets toned down.
changes: Settings > Display > Flashes: Full (default), Low, Off. Saved with your settings.
It scales the x5 strobe, the sky and rim flash, the bloom swell and the drop's juice glow; lasers dim to 35% at Off. Callouts, speed lines, particles and music are untouched.
images: The new Flashes row in Settings > Display
checks: measured over the same 6 s combo (frame mean brightness): Full 5 flashes, biggest jump 91; Low 3 flashes, biggest jump 36; Off 0 flashes, biggest jump 4
clicking the row cycles Full -> Low and saves to gemstogether-settings-v1
verify 22/22

title: Round 6 (patch 11): Resonance, a shared Zone-style meter
why: Tetris Effect Connected's big idea: both players fill one meter together and share one climax. Our co-op had no shared goal.
beforeLabel: patch 10: the same kind of session, no meter
afterLabel: patch 11: the meter fills, RESONANCE fires, 8 s of concert, then the payout
changes: Every cleared gem charges one shared meter (60 gems, plus 12 per stage). In co-op both players' clears count, and the bar shows your share and your partner's share in your colours.

When it fills: RESONANCE (or TEAM RESONANCE if you both put in at least 20%). 8 seconds of concert: lasers pinned, maximum flow, golden light around the screen edges, light chasing the frame, every clear rings a chord that climbs, and the full soundtrack plays.
Then the payout: 'N GEMS  RESONANCE COMPLETE' with twelve fireworks and a crown fountain.
A tier callout now lifts above a stage card when both land at once.
checks: tools/coop-res.mjs (two real browsers, private room): after each host and peer move both screens show the same meter and the mirrored split, 10/10
verify 22/22, coop-point 10/10, swap-audit solo/host/peer pass

title: Round 7 (patch 12): clears land on the beat
why: The core Tetris Effect trick: what you do sounds like it's in time with the music.
changes: Match, special and chord sounds wait for the next 1/32 of the soundtrack's grid (never more than about 90 ms at 84 BPM, less on faster stages). Swaps, clicks and the reject buzz are never delayed, so input stays instant.
images: Measured from AudioBufferSourceNode.start() in a real-time session: before 0/23 result sounds on the grid, after 23/23 (longest wait 74 ms)
checks: tools/beat-audit.mjs: after 23/23 on the grid, before 0/23, 0 errors

title: Round 8 (patch 13): optional run end
why: Andre: 'some kind of fail-state would be nice, like out of moves'. Tront: 'would want a toggle for people who would rather flip the board'.
beforeLabel: patch 12: no moves left, it reshuffles
afterLabel: patch 13 with End run on: OUT OF MOVES card
changes: Settings > Display > Out of moves: Reshuffle (default) or End run. Only when no partner is connected, so it never ends a shared board.
End run: the board dims, the card slides in, your score counts up, the stage you reached, NEW BEST! with fireworks, and a Play again button. The soundtrack drops to just the pad.

title: Round 10 (patch 14): the board breathes to the beat
why: Tetris Effect's pieces pulse with the music (its Mino Strobe setting), and the research says the environment should join in from x3. Before this, the board ignored the soundtrack.
changes: The frame glows in the stage colour on every beat: harder on downbeats and as flow rises. It uses the soundtrack's own beat times, or a game-time clock when the sound is off.
Gems bump about 2% on the beat (off with reduced motion).
A chain of x3 or more holds a tier-coloured aura around the frame; it goes rainbow during Resonance.
checks: verify 22/22

title: Round 11 (patch 15): the research pass, x5 crosses a state boundary
why: Deep research (research/DEEP-RESEARCH-COMBO-SPECTACLE.md): 'Do not make 5x merely five times as loud as 1x. Make 5x cross a state boundary that 1x cannot access.' Recommended: x4 = transformation warning; x5 = exclusive phrase, a short mix duck then impact, slow-time or a presentation hold, a distinct haptic envelope; cycle excitation and relaxation; unique names for exceptional results (Dodecatris).
afterLabel: patch 15 (same fixture; x5 lands at about 5.3 s)
changes: x4: a noise riser climbs toward the next step (the transformation warning).

The first x5 of a chain is the climax, with assets nothing else uses: the music ducks for a quarter second, then slams back with an exclusive eight-note fanfare, a crash and a sub impact; game time drops to 0.3x for 0.45 s (a presentation hold); gold shock rings; the longest rumble.
The strobe runs on real time, so it stays a sharp 160 ms hit even inside the slow motion.
After any x5+ chain the soundtrack exhales: pad only for two bars, then it builds again.
Resonance payouts are named by size: RADIANT RESONANCE (35+), PRISMATIC RESONANCE (60+), SUPERNOVA (90+).
checks: clip log: game time runs at 0.3x through the x5 hold (0.04 s per 4 frames against 0.133), then recovers
verify 22/22
